title: bug: live-goal-release.test.tsx reds the whole control-room lane under suite load but passes 3/3 alone
description:
Filed by worker-bcaa6d5e from parent task-2a345b2e97d94599b4688af1923056e5 (Gate 3 roll-up, step 3 gate run, 2026-09-08T20:0xZ). NOT a defect of that parent — its diff is empty — and NOT a defect of any of its three children; measured to task-3697c02bf2ab41a896fcfacb125d9e46.

REPRO. `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` at HEAD 8b785725:
  Test Files  1 failed | 204 passed (205)
       Tests  1 failed | 2676 passed (2677)
  FAIL src/v2/goals/live-goal-release.test.tsx > the refusal path is unchanged by the fix > keeps a transport abort and a daemon refusal at different codes AND different layers
  TestingLibraryElementError: Unable to find an element by: [data-testid="cr.release.answer"]
Reproduced 2/2 full-suite runs (23:01:05 and 23:01:53 local). The SAME file run alone passes 3/3: `cd apps/control-room && npx vitest run src/v2/goals/live-goal-release.test.tsx` => `Test Files 1 passed (1)` / `Tests 4 passed (4)`, three consecutive times.

DIAGNOSIS FROM THE DUMP, not inferred. The rendered DOM in the failure is the card MID-SUBMIT: the button reads `Recording your decision...` and is `disabled`, and `cr.release.base` is `disabled` — i.e. `busy === true`. `cr.release.answer` only renders once `answer !== null`, so the helper at live-goal-release.test.tsx:211 `screen.getByTestId("cr.release.answer").querySelector("code")` is a SYNCHRONOUS read taken before the submit promise has settled. Called from :284. Under an otherwise-idle machine the microtask drains before the assertion; under full-suite load it does not. Same class as gotcha-a-5s-default-timeout-flake-is-contention-not-work. Likely fix: `await screen.findByTestId("cr.release.answer")` (or wrap the click in `await act`) instead of the sync `getByTestId` — a test-only change; no evidence the production card is wrong.

OWNERSHIP MEASURED. `git log -- apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/live-goal-release.test.tsx` returns exactly ONE commit, 2569dd4e (task-3697c02b, "bug: a live release.decide outruns the browser's 15s transport abort"), authored 2026-09-08 21:40:21 +0300 = 18:40:21Z. The file is CLEAN at HEAD (`git status --porcelain` on it is empty), so this is landed bytes, not peer dirt. That commit is 35 minutes AFTER task-817d893f's completion 00c88cd8 (18:05:17Z, control-room `Test Files 204 passed (204)` / `Tests 2673 passed (2673)` EXIT 0), which is why the Gate 3 children's own green gates never saw it.

WHY IT ESCAPED ITS OWN ROW'S GATE: task-3697c02b's recorded verification is `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room exec vitest run --exclude src/live/live-runs.test.ts` => 204 files / 2621 tests EXIT 0. That run EXCLUDES a file and lands 204/2621 against the full lane's 205/2677, so it is not the lane gate its DoD stands on. Worth pinning in the fix: the gate for a control-room row is the unexcluded `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`.

DoD SUGGESTION: make the assertion await the answer, then prove non-vacuity — the arm must still go RED when the production `answer` state is mutated to swallow the refusal code/layer distinction (rail 1: assert the code AND which layer refused, not merely that it refused), and quote an unexcluded `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` count line at 205 files.
definitionOfDone: `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` (NO --exclude) is EXIT 0 with its `Test Files N passed` count line quoted verbatim at 205 files / 2677+ tests, run twice consecutively so a load-dependent flake cannot pass once by luck.

The repaired arm is proven non-vacuous by mutation: make the production `live-goal-release.tsx` answer path collapse the transport-abort code/layer into the daemon-refusal code/layer and confirm the arm goes RED, then restore and prove the restore by SHA256 against an out-of-tree backup keyed on BOTH the task id and the worker id, in a call separate from the restore.

No production behaviour change is made unless a defect in `live-goal-release.tsx` is actually measured; if the fix is test-only, say so explicitly in the completion record rather than editing the component to make a test pass.

THE LANE GATE, TWICE, UNEXCLUDED (DoD 1).

Run `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` — NO `--exclude` — twice consecutively, and quote the exit code and the `Test Files N passed` count line VERBATIM for each run. THE COUNT IN DoD 1 IS A REFERENCE, NOT A LITERAL TO MATCH. It says "205 files / 2677+ tests", but epic rail 3 forbids freezing a roster count precisely because concurrent rows move these numbers. Take the PRINTED count as authoritative: a HIGHER count satisfies the clause and should be reported as such with a one-line note that a sibling row added tests. Only a LOWER file count, or any nonzero failed count, is a failure. Read the OUTPUT, not the exit code — a run that matched no files prints "No test files found" and exits 0.

Run at least one of the two under real contention if you can arrange it. Two green runs on a quiet host are consistent with the flake still being present; what makes them meaningful is that the drain is deterministic, so say which runs were loaded and which were quiet.

This is one package's lane and it does not need the root suite. `pnpm test` would not cover it anyway — the root vitest include has no `apps/**` — so do not quote a root count as evidence for this clause. If you also run other legs, label them; this DoD is about the control-room lane.

  AssertionError: expected +0 to be 1

`expect(wire.sends()).toBe(1)` is a SYNCHRONOUS COUNTER READ of the same detached chain, and it is strictly EARLIER in that chain than anything I had drained: `spendOffer` hashes the payload with `crypto.subtle.digest` BEFORE it calls `sendCommand`, so `sends` does not move until that threadpool round trip lands. My step-3 `slow-boundary` drill could not catch it because it delays AFTER `wire.submit` returns, by which time `sends` has already incremented.

Two sites were unguarded (:270, :298); three more (:191, :323, :334) were already covered by preceding drains. Added `sendCount(wire)` on the same bounded-drain pattern and routed ALL FIVE through it — the three safe ones cost zero drains, and uniformity means a future line reorder cannot silently reintroduce the flake.

=== B. A FIFTH DEFECT, ORDERING NOT DRAINING, FOUND BY A SHARPER DRILL ===
Added a `slow-dispatch` mutation that delays BEFORE `wire.submit` (where the real digest sits). It still red the last arm with element-not-found, and the cause is different in kind: that arm did `await settle(TRANSPORT_BOUND_MS)` to fire an abort armed by `setTimeout` INSIDE `sendCommand`. If the dispatch has not happened yet, the clock advances past a timer THAT DOES NOT EXIST, and no later 0ms drain can ever fire it — an unfixable-by-draining stall. Fixed by ORDERING: assert the send (which drains) BEFORE moving the clock. Commented in place so it is not "tidied" back.
